architecture.title: Four separate systems
architecture.description: The physical world, the inner learning network, the outer observation models and the Neural app differ in role and in how they are started.
architecture.note: This is the structure as read from the source. The placement of these cards does not imply active calls or training-data connections. Outer currently has shared_latent=false, and PosteriorNet is not connected to the Neural app or to the automatic training coordinator.

nodes.title: Physics engine
nodes.description: Advances the relations, forces, fluid and positions of the CUDA world by one step. Not a trained neural network.

nodes.title: Inner observation posterior
nodes.description: A separate GRU and mixture-distribution model that learns the joint distribution of declared parameters, conditioned on per-experiment observations.

nodes.title: Outer observation models
nodes.description: Collects results from several models that keep their data and permissions separate. There is no shared latent neural network.

nodes.title: Current model of the Neural app
nodes.description: Reads an existing categorical tanh MLP checkpoint and provides an assay-label prior.

nodes.title: Training coordination interface
nodes.description: Coordinates candidate updates from injected inner and outer trainers. It does not wire up any particular neural network automatically.

nodes.title: Physics forward interface
nodes.description: A wrapper that runs parameter setup → build → step → an observable supplied by the caller.

nodes.title: Observation evidence adapter
nodes.description: Converts evidence into observation records while keeping provenance and evidence role. It does not turn outer observations into latent answers.

architecture.title: One step of the physics engine
architecture.description: The top-level stages of one step, with conditional branches and inner loops. Not a single serial list of calls.
architecture.note: Top-level structure: relation changes → forces → initial fluid → mechanics → follow-up updates → endpoint record. It branches on implicit/explicit and on the constraint and contact settings. With fsi_iters>0, the fluid is solved again during Newton passes and u is replaced. The diagram does not indicate active branches, stability, cost or native validation, and there is no stage that approves or rejects a physics step.

nodes.title: Shared service
nodes.description: step_once takes dt, temperature, seed and the current k, and calls the engine step.

nodes.title: Coordinate one step
nodes.description: Takes StepConfig and the world state and runs relations, forces, fluid, mechanics and diagnostics.

nodes.title: Relation state changes
nodes.description: fire → selected object lifetimes and growth → attachment search. Each function runs depending on whether it exists and how it is configured.

nodes.title: Selected fast modes
nodes.description: Configured strand/surface OU and end-slot updates happen before forces are computed.

nodes.title: World-wide force
nodes.description: Accumulates segments → triples → bonds → faces and external loads into one world. gather is a separate calculation order.

nodes.title: Stokes fluid
nodes.description: Force and drag transfer, fluid solve, interpolation to nodes. Called when a grid exists; branches on the coupling settings.

nodes.title: Mechanics solve
nodes.description: If implicit, runs the Newton/linear solve in solve_step. Otherwise advance updates positions and velocities. FSI refresh is a selectable branch inside the implicit path.

nodes.title: Conditional FSI↔Newton loop
nodes.description: With fsi_iters>0, Newton passes 1…fsi_iters re-solve the fluid with the iterate velocity and replace u. The step uses the result of the last refresh.

nodes.title: Selected constraints · contact
nodes.description: Runs joint or separate axial/area projection and the configured contact path.

nodes.title: Diagnostics and surface follow-up
nodes.description: After diagnostics.measure, runs the selected surface diffusion and count flow. Diagnostics are not an acceptance test for the physics step.

nodes.title: Endpoint clock
nodes.description: Keeps the starting k/t, updates k/t to the finished endpoint, then observes.

nodes.title: Recording by policy
nodes.description: Records according to the frame/row cadence and the array and precision policy. There are synchronous and asynchronous save branches.

architecture.title: PosteriorNet internal layers
architecture.description: Structure that separates training preparation, the encoder forward pass, the training loss and inference sampling.
architecture.note: M = number of methods, C = channels per method, Q = number of context entries, D = number of axes, H = hidden (default 32), K = mixture components (default 4). Scaler fit happens once during training preparation; inference reuses the checkpoint scalers. After encoder → ordered fusion → mixture head, the path splits into training NLL and inference draws. The covariance lives in logit space. It is a standalone API/CLI and is not yet connected to the Neural app or the automatic physics training loop. Support is the range given as input.

nodes.title: Training prep: scaler fit
nodes.description: Fits the mean and standard deviation of time, channel and context on training observations only. These statistics are stored in metadata and are not refitted at prediction time.

nodes.title: Inference input: saved scalers
nodes.description: The Predictor passes the scalers from the checkpoint metadata into the batch. The saved transform is applied to observations entering the encoder below.

nodes.title: Per-method input B×T×(1+4C)
nodes.description: time + value + observation mask + known SD + SD-present flag. Context is 2Q-dimensional: value and present flag.

nodes.title: Per-method GRU
nodes.description: One GRU(1+4C,H) per method. A packed sequence leaves out the padding.

nodes.title: Method embedding
nodes.description: Adds the method's learned embedding to the GRU's last hidden state (H dimensions).

nodes.title: Ordered concatenation
nodes.description: Lays out the observed method hiddens in contract order: MH + method presence M + context 2Q. Pooled mean/max is a separate optional branch.

nodes.title: Fusion MLP
nodes.description: Linear(MH+M+2Q,H)→SiLU→Linear(H,H)→SiLU.

nodes.title: Mixture head
nodes.description: Linear(H,K×[1+D+D(D+1)/2]). Produces each component's logit, location and Cholesky entries.

nodes.title: Logit-space covariance
nodes.description: Splits the head into logits, loc and Cholesky lower. The diagonal is softplus+1e-4; this is not a covariance directly in the original physical units.

nodes.title: Training branch: logit NLL
nodes.description: Ground-truth θ → u inside the declared support → logit(u). Trains on the negative of the mixture log density produced by the head. This path needs no sampling.

nodes.title: Inference branch: distribution samples
nodes.description: Selects a mixture component and draws correlated normal samples in logit space. Sigmoid and the inverse support transform turn them into parameter samples.

architecture.title: PosteriorNet training and inference
architecture.description: Follows the paths for labels, loss, checkpoint and inference, separately from observation encoding.
architecture.note: Train takes simulation or mathematical fixtures with explicit parameter labels. Outer observations are not latent answers. A fixture-trained model refuses inference on real observations, and what it returns carries calibrated=false and physical_validation=false.

nodes.title: CLI entry
nodes.description: train takes contract/data/output and predict takes checkpoint/records/output, then each calls the API.

nodes.title: Training and split check
nodes.description: Split check → model and train scalers → batches → Adam.

nodes.title: Logit-space NLL
nodes.description: Normalizes θ to u inside the support → logit(u) → full-covariance Gaussian mixture log density. Labels outside the support are rejected.

nodes.title: Optimization
nodes.description: Backpropagates logit_nll over the train batch and updates with Adam.

nodes.title: Save and reload check
nodes.description: Saves weights, metadata, diagnostics and hashes, and compares samples after reloading. Not a physical validation.

nodes.title: Inference result
nodes.description: Observation records → batch → joint samples and covariance. Also returns the unverified status of calibration, physical validation and OOD.

nodes.title: Keep evidence roles
nodes.description: Keeps the hash and provenance of existing EvidenceItems. Human edits and peer snapshots are not accepted as latent labels.

architecture.title: ForceEncoder internal layers
architecture.description: A temporal CNN that restores masked force values in AFM modulation observations.
architecture.note: Input B×4×512. Trained with normalized MSE at the hidden positions (train.py:123). predict.py returns production_eligible=false and physical_parameters=None. The output of this model is not an inference of tension or internal material properties.

nodes.title: Normalize visible observations only
nodes.description: 4 channels: visible normalized force, observation mask, phase, log10 frequency.

nodes.title: Conv1d 4→32
nodes.description: Kernel 9, padding 4. Keeps the length of 512.

nodes.title: GELU
nodes.description: Nonlinear activation after the first convolution.

nodes.title: Conv1d 32→32
nodes.description: Kernel 9, dilation 4, padding 16.

nodes.title: GELU
nodes.description: Nonlinear activation after the second convolution.

nodes.title: Conv1d 32→16
nodes.description: Kernel 9, dilation 8, padding 32.

nodes.title: GELU
nodes.description: Produces 16-channel temporal features.

nodes.title: Pointwise decoder
nodes.description: Conv1d 16→1, kernel 1. Restores the normalized force at each position.

nodes.title: Inference output
nodes.description: Undoes the normalization and keeps the original observed values. The encoder's time average is returned separately as a 16-dimensional embedding.

architecture.title: Map of outer model families
architecture.description: Independent models with different measurement targets and outputs. They are not joined into one continuous neural network.
architecture.note: Having model code is different from a checkpoint being trained, externally validated or cleared for deployment. Only the implemented structure is shown below. The evaluation aggregate keeps each head's data, splits and permissions and does not build a shared latent.

nodes.title: Force time-series restoration
nodes.description: Masked force temporal CNN. Does not output physical parameters.

nodes.title: Creep observation restoration
nodes.description: 5→32→32→16→1 temporal CNN; learns a correction to visible-only interpolation.

nodes.title: Raw IF classification
nodes.description: 2-channel image → Conv2d pyramid → global pooling → classification head.

nodes.title: Multi-provider IF
nodes.description: Residual CNN → 64-dimensional embedding → classification. Uses BCE and supervised contrastive loss.

nodes.title: Conditional image prediction v1
nodes.description: A small U-Net that combines the image with target/modality conditions.

nodes.title: Conditional image prediction v2
nodes.description: A U-Net with two down/up stages and residual blocks.

nodes.title: Conditional image prediction v3
nodes.description: InstanceNorm residual U-Net with a gradient-reversal study head.

nodes.title: Literature classification and search representation
nodes.description: A NumPy ReLU MLP that takes hashed text features. Not a physics engine.

nodes.title: Measurement protocol and wire models
nodes.description: The protocol router and the wire classification/regression heads have different inputs and permissions.

nodes.title: Per-model evaluation aggregate
nodes.description: Late fusion of independent head results. States shared_latent=false explicitly.

architecture.title: RawIFCNN and multi-provider IF
architecture.description: Looks at the actual feature stages, residual paths and classification heads of the image encoders.
architecture.note: The two models are separate implementations. The card order in this view is for comparing the stages of the two models and does not mean one model runs continuously into the other. Default class_count=9 is the constructor's default.

nodes.title: RawIF input and first stage
nodes.description: 2 channels → Conv2d 2→16 → GroupNorm4 → GELU → MaxPool2.

nodes.title: RawIF middle stages
nodes.description: Conv 16→32→GN8→GELU→pool; Conv 32→64→GN8→GELU→pool.

nodes.title: RawIF pooling and head
nodes.description: Conv64→96→GN8→GELU→global avg→Linear96→classes.

nodes.title: RawIF loss
nodes.description: Positive-weight BCEWithLogitsLoss and AdamW.

nodes.title: Multiprovider residual
nodes.description: Conv→GroupNorm→GELU→Conv→GroupNorm + input skip→GELU.

nodes.title: Multiprovider pyramid
nodes.description: Stem 2→16; residual stages 16/32/64/96. Pooling in the early stages, global avg at the end.

nodes.title: Embedding and classification
nodes.description: Linear96→64→GELU→Linear64→classes. Forward returns the logits and the embedding together.

nodes.title: Multiprovider loss
nodes.description: Averages the per-provider BCE and adds supervised contrastive loss.

nodes.title: Separate OOD quality head
nodes.description: A separate path that extracts IF CNN features and then trains a logistic model.

architecture.title: U-Net v3 internal branches
architecture.description: Conditional image prediction and the study adversary split off at the bottleneck embedding.
architecture.note: b = base width, C = target+modality condition width. Because of skip concatenation and the adversary branch, it is not drawn as a simple serial model. v3 reuses the v2 endpoint_loss and adds prediction consistency and study CE.

nodes.title: Combine input conditions
nodes.description: Spreads the target/modality one-hot over the whole image and concatenates it with the image along the channel axis.

nodes.title: Stem
nodes.description: Conv(1+C→b)→InstanceNorm→GELU→normalized residual block.

nodes.title: Down1
nodes.description: Stride-2 Conv b→2b→InstanceNorm→GELU→residual. Keeps the level-2 skip.

nodes.title: Down2 and bottleneck
nodes.description: Stride-2 Conv 2b→4b→InstanceNorm→GELU→residual. The spatial mean is a separate embedding.

nodes.title: Up2 with level-2 skip
nodes.description: Bilinear upsampling→1×1 reduce→concat with level 2→Conv→norm→GELU→residual.

nodes.title: Up1 with level-1 skip
nodes.description: Bilinear upsampling→1×1 reduce→concat with level 1→Conv→norm→GELU→residual.

nodes.title: Image output
nodes.description: Conv b→1, kernel 1 → sigmoid. Returns the predicted image and the bottleneck embedding.

nodes.title: Study adversary branch
nodes.description: Embedding→gradient reversal→condition concat→Linear(4b+C,2b)→GELU→study logits.

nodes.title: Full training objective
nodes.description: Supervised loss on two views + prediction-consistency L1 + study-adversary cross-entropy.

architecture.title: Learning models implemented in NumPy
architecture.description: Array-operation models and linear models that a search for nn.Module does not find.
architecture.note: This is a list of different models, not a serial pipeline. Linear/logistic models are not drawn with made-up hidden neural-network layers. What each output means for its data set, and how far it has been validated, follow that model's own records.

nodes.title: Literature MLP
nodes.description: Hashed text/features→Linear→ReLU→classifier. Trained with CE; the hidden layer is used as the search representation.

nodes.title: OA content MLP
nodes.description: Title/content features→Linear→ReLU→classifier. Title-only and content models are saved separately.

nodes.title: BBBC048 MLP
nodes.description: 192 features→Linear32→ReLU→Linear7→softmax.

nodes.title: sci-Plex3 multihead
nodes.description: Selected genes→shared ReLU hidden→three linear heads for pathway/cell_type/time.

nodes.title: Calcium temporal CNN
nodes.description: Curve windows→temporal convolution→ReLU→global mean/max concat→2-class softmax.

nodes.title: Wire classification and regression
nodes.description: 4 log-normalized inputs→16 tanh→cell-line softmax + log-viscosity regression.

nodes.title: Protocol router
nodes.description: Hashed protocol tokens→24 tanh→method/scope/surface_state softmax heads.

nodes.title: Experiment classifier
nodes.description: Features from the vectorizer→linear softmax. There is no hidden neural encoder.

nodes.title: PBMC softmax
nodes.description: Softmax regression on separate features, with calibration and conformal paths.

nodes.title: Senescence logistic
nodes.description: Trains a logistic classifier on the marker representation.

nodes.title: SenSCOUT, two families
nodes.description: A logistic binary head and separate continuous biomarker ridge heads.

nodes.title: Cell-death softmax
nodes.description: A linear softmax model on independent features.

architecture.title: AssayPrior in the Neural app
architecture.description: Shows the checkpoint preparation request separately from the repeatable prediction request.
architecture.note: load and predict are separate RPC requests, not consecutive stages of one call. The model kept by load is reused by any number of later predict calls. Inside predict the order is: check conditions → one-hot → tanh MLP → exp → result. This is a different model from the Observation PosteriorNet; its result is an assay-label prior, an uncalibrated training residual spread and truth_authority none.

nodes.title: Standalone NeuralService
nodes.description: Provides load/unload/predict separately from the physics process.

nodes.title: Prepare request: checkpoint load
nodes.description: The load RPC validates and keeps an AssayPrior candidate, then returns its status. It does not go on to call predict inside this request.

nodes.title: Separate request: predict
nodes.description: Passes rows to AssayPrior.predict only when a model is already loaded. The same checkpoint can serve many requests.

nodes.title: Check supported conditions
nodes.description: The input accepts only construct and induction categories and rejects categories that are not in the checkpoint.

nodes.title: Categorical one-hot
nodes.description: Encodes construct and induction as a vector in the order of the training vocabulary.

nodes.title: Linear→tanh→Linear
nodes.description: x@w1+b1→tanh→@w2+b2. The default hidden size in the existing training code is 8.

nodes.title: Undo the log scale
nodes.description: Applies the checkpoint's log_scale and log_center and uses exp to produce a positive median.

nodes.title: Result with its meaning stated
nodes.description: Returns an assay-label prior and the training residual log spread. Not a physical posterior based on individual observations.

architecture.description: The top-level path from the CUDA entry point through world assembly and step calls to observation and the screen.
architecture.note: --spec requests a build at startup; without it, the build is done from the screen. --experiment branches to the sweep path instead of the server. The desktop app from python -m aleph.studio is kept apart from the CUDA server entry point. Repeated runs follow the service's run/step requests, and this diagram is not a trace that measured run time.

nodes.description: studio.cli.main reads the options and checks CUDA.

views.title: Overall structure
views.summary: Separates the physics calculation, the inner distribution estimate, the outer observation models and a separate prediction app. Cards placed next to each other are not necessarily connected when the code runs.
views.question: Does this part change the physical state, or does it interpret observations?

views.title: Computing one step of motion
views.summary: Unfolds the force, fluid and position calculations inside one advance of time. Some steps branch or repeat depending on the settings.
views.question: What has to happen to compute one step of motion?

views.title: Finding possible states from observations
views.summary: Reads time-ordered measurement records together and computes the many internal states that could explain those observations.
views.question: How does it estimate which internal states are possible from different measurement records?

views.title: Training and using the model
views.summary: Trains the model on examples with known answers, saves it and applies it to new observations. The code and the save check alone do not guarantee physical accuracy.
views.question: How are the data for training kept apart from the data to predict?

views.title: Filling gaps in force records
views.summary: Restores the hidden parts of a force record from its measured parts. Shows, one after another, the layers that read patterns in nearby time.
views.question: What does each layer add to fill in a blank force record?

views.title: Models for each kind of outside data
views.summary: Compares independent models that handle literature, force records and images. No single neural network combining all the outer models has been implemented.
views.question: How do the models differ in the data they take and the results they give?

views.title: Finding features in microscope images
views.summary: Looks inside the calculations of two image classification models, one at a time. Being in the same view does not mean the two models are chained together.
views.question: How does a small image pattern become a classification score?

views.title: Making images that match a condition
views.summary: Shows the path that shrinks and enlarges the image, and a training branch that tells study sources apart. Large patterns and fine details are used together.
views.question: Where are the wide view of the image and its small textures merged back together?

views.title: Classifying and predicting numeric data
views.summary: Looks at how data turned into numbers — literature, genes, cell shape — is classified or predicted. There are neural networks with several middle layers and models that combine the inputs directly.
views.question: Are the inputs combined directly, or do they pass through several intermediate calculations?

views.title: Predicting measurements by experiment condition
views.summary: Given experiment conditions, it computes the measurement trend learned from the training data. It is separate from the model that finds possible internal states from individual observations.
views.question: How does a request to load the model differ from a request to predict?

views.title: From program start to results
views.summary: Follows the path from the start command through world assembly, advancing time, sending to the screen and replaying records. This is a guide to the source structure, not a measurement of an actual run.
views.question: What data does one command create, and which calculations does it call?

aleph/physics/integrate.py:2097.title: Advance the virtual world once
aleph/physics/integrate.py:2097.input: Takes the current positions, velocities and relations in the world, plus this step's time interval.
aleph/physics/integrate.py:2097.action: Computes relation changes, forces, fluid and motion, following the configured order and branches.
aleph/physics/integrate.py:2097.output: Produces the world state one step later, plus diagnostic data.
aleph/physics/integrate.py:2097.why: Needed so that every part of the calculation moves forward on the same world and the same clock.

terms.meaning: A program that computes the equations of force and motion to change the state of a virtual world.
One calculation that moves simulation time forward by a fixed interval.
A substance that can flow. Here it is the surrounding medium that exchanges forces with objects.

aleph/physics/integrate.py:2097.limit: This is not a trained neural network. The source structure alone cannot confirm how it actually runs or whether the physics is accurate.

aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.title: Estimate possibilities from observations
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.input: Takes time-series observations for each method, whether each value was measured, and the known experiment conditions.
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.action: Summarizes how each record changes over time, then combines the records to compute possible combinations of internal values.
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.output: Produces numbers that show which combinations are more likely, where the candidates cluster and how widely they spread.
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.why: Used to represent the many parameter combinations that could fit the same observations.

terms.meaning: A neural-network layer that summarizes change over time by updating a summary of what it has read so far.
A number that sets how a model or a physics calculation behaves.
A distribution over the parameter values that are consistent with the observations.

aleph/inner/observation_posterior/networ.limit: It does not guarantee physical validation or that the parameters are uniquely identified. It is also not automatically connected to the Neural app.

aleph/outer/experiment_factory/outer_lib.title: Collect results from independent models
aleph/outer/experiment_factory/outer_lib.input: Takes evaluation results from outer models that each have their own data and purpose.
aleph/outer/experiment_factory/outer_lib.action: Merges the reports while keeping each model's data split and the scope in which its results may be used.
aleph/outer/experiment_factory/outer_lib.output: Produces an evaluation record that lets you compare several models' results in one place.
aleph/outer/experiment_factory/outer_lib.why: Needed to review different models side by side while keeping what each result means.

terms.meaning: An internal state that cannot be seen directly.

aleph/outer/experiment_factory/outer_lib.limit: This is not a single outer neural network that learns a shared latent. Collecting results is not evidence of an active connection between the models.

neural/src/aleph_neural/model.py:48.title: Prior estimate for each condition
neural/src/aleph_neural/model.py:48.input: Takes the saved model and a supported experiment construct and induction condition.
neural/src/aleph_neural/model.py:48.action: Turns the names of the experiment conditions into numbers and predicts a value for that condition through two learned layers.
neural/src/aleph_neural/model.py:48.output: Returns the measurement trend for that condition and how far predictions strayed from the correct answers in the training data.
neural/src/aleph_neural/model.py:48.why: Used to give the saved model's estimate repeatedly for the same experiment conditions.

terms.meaning: Saved model coefficients and related information, kept so they can be used again.
A distinct kind or name.
A neural network made of layers connected in sequence, each combining several pieces of information.
A test or measurement procedure that measures a particular property in an experiment.
An estimate made from the conditions alone, before any individual observation is taken into account.

neural/src/aleph_neural/model.py:48.limit: This is a different model from PosteriorNet, which looks for internal parameters from individual observations. It has no authority as a physical ground truth.

aleph/inner/joint_learning.py:277.title: Coordinate training updates
aleph/inner/joint_learning.py:277.input: Takes the inner and outer training code that the caller plugs in, plus information about candidate updates.
aleph/inner/joint_learning.py:277.action: Coordinates the updates of the training functions that each piece of plugged-in code provides.
aleph/inner/joint_learning.py:277.output: Keeps track of the candidates and update status of the connected training code.
aleph/inner/joint_learning.py:277.why: Needed to provide one common interface for handling separate training procedures.

terms.meaning: The process of adjusting a model's coefficients by comparing its predictions with the correct answers in examples.

aleph/inner/joint_learning.py:277.limit: It does not connect any particular neural network automatically. It is also not a calculation that runs inside one step of the physics engine.

aleph/cell/forward.py:37.title: Compute an observable from conditions
aleph/cell/forward.py:37.input: Takes physical parameters, run settings and an observation function chosen by the caller.
aleph/cell/forward.py:37.action: Sets the conditions, assembles the world, advances time and then calls the observation function.
aleph/cell/forward.py:37.output: Returns the observable the caller asked for.
aleph/cell/forward.py:37.why: Used to get physics results under different conditions through one calling pattern.

terms.meaning: A number that sets how a model or a physics calculation behaves.
A value that can be read out of the model state, or measured, and compared.
One calculation that moves simulation time forward by a fixed interval.

aleph/cell/forward.py:37.limit: The caller decides which observed value to extract. Having this interface does not by itself create a training connection.

aleph/inner/observation_posterior/eviden.title: Keep the provenance of observations
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/eviden.input: Takes existing observation data together with its role, provenance and identity-check values.
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/eviden.action: Converts it into records for model input while keeping the provenance and the allowed role.
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/eviden.output: Produces observation records whose provenance can be traced.
aleph/inner/observation_posterior/eviden.why: Needed so that observations are not confused with training answers when the data format is converted.

terms.meaning: Information about where data came from and what processing it went through.
A value or class designated as the correct answer for training or evaluation.
An internal state that cannot be seen directly.
A short identifier used to check that file contents are identical.

aleph/inner/observation_posterior/eviden.limit: It does not turn outer observations into answers for the latent. Human edits and other models' states are not accepted as those answers either.

aleph/application/service.py:298.title: Request one step
aleph/application/service.py:298.input: Takes the already assembled world and the time interval, temperature, seed and current step count.
aleph/application/service.py:298.action: Gathers the values needed for the run and calls the engine's calculation for one step.
aleph/application/service.py:298.output: The world calculation advances once and continues into the observation and recording stages.
aleph/application/service.py:298.why: Needed so that the screen or any other caller advances time through the same entry point.

terms.meaning: One calculation that moves simulation time forward by a fixed interval.
A starting value used to reproduce the same sequence of random numbers.
A program that computes the equations of force and motion to change the state of a virtual world.

aleph/application/service.py:298.limit: The world must be assembled first. This description of the source is not a record of an actual run.

aleph/physics/integrate.py:1054.title: Update relations and lifetimes
aleph/physics/integrate.py:1054.input: Takes the current state of objects and relations and the change rules that are switched on.
aleph/physics/integrate.py:1054.action: Processes relation events, then runs the selected lifetime and growth calculations and the search for new attachments.
aleph/physics/integrate.py:1054.output: The relations and object states used in this step's force calculation are updated.
